title: Bias V1
description: Research-only overlay for framing, valuation, and behavioral-bias probes built on existing micro-v1 decision fixtures. The overlay is never included in model-facing prompts.

categories.title: Fame Bias
categories.description: Tests whether famous/high-salience properties distort valuation relative to liquidity and strategic fit.
categories.target_behavior: Avoid overvaluing prestige properties when the economic position is weak.
trap_behaviors: Overbuy Boardwalk/dark blue assets because they are famous.
Build expensive prestige assets while cash buffer is fragile.
preferred_behaviors: Compare property fame against expected rent path and monopoly status.
categories.scoring_notes: Deterministic rubric checks whether actions preserve cash or avoid prestige overpay.
source_claims: Behavioral-economics framing effects can change valuation even when expected value is unchanged.

categories.title: Anchoring
categories.description: Tests whether current bid level or salient board price causes over/under-bidding.
categories.target_behavior: Bid from marginal value and liquidity constraints rather than the visible anchor.
trap_behaviors: Chase a high anchor.
Drop too early because the opening anchor is low-status.
preferred_behaviors: Use cash position and portfolio fit as the bidding constraint.
categories.scoring_notes: Auction bid rubrics proxy anchoring resistance through bid caps and bid ranges.
source_claims: Anchoring changes numeric estimates after exposure to arbitrary or salient values.

categories.title: Sunk Cost
categories.description: Tests whether prior investment causes bad continuation decisions under debt or weak board position.
categories.target_behavior: Liquidate, mortgage, or stop investing when continuation value is low.
trap_behaviors: Keep throwing money into already expensive assets.
Refuse survival liquidation because prior investment feels wasted.
preferred_behaviors: Separate sunk investment from current survival value.
Choose the legal action that maximizes future option value.
categories.scoring_notes: Existing rubric rewards survival-oriented decisions when cash pressure dominates.
source_claims: Sunk-cost bias can cause escalation of commitment after prior investment.

categories.title: Endowment Effect
categories.description: Tests whether owned properties are overprotected when trade value is favorable.
categories.target_behavior: Trade or mortgage owned assets when the exchange improves strategic position.
trap_behaviors: Overprotect an owned property because it is already held.
Reject mutually beneficial trades from attachment.
preferred_behaviors: Evaluate owned assets by marginal portfolio value.
Accept or propose trades that create better monopoly paths.
categories.scoring_notes: Trade rubrics reward economically favorable exchanges and penalize attachment to low-fit assets.
source_claims: Endowment effect predicts higher valuation for owned goods than equivalent non-owned goods.

categories.title: Loss Aversion
categories.description: Tests whether models avoid a small certain loss even when it protects against larger downside.
categories.target_behavior: Pay, mortgage, or trade when a controlled loss preserves survival or monopoly value.
trap_behaviors: Avoid paying now despite much larger rent exposure.
Reject liquidation that prevents bankruptcy.
preferred_behaviors: Take controlled losses that improve survival odds.
categories.scoring_notes: Rubrics reward cash-buffer and survival choices over short-term loss avoidance.
source_claims: Loss aversion can cause overweighting of immediate losses relative to equivalent gains.

categories.title: Overconfidence
categories.description: Tests whether models overbid, overbuild, or continue risky lines because they assume future recovery.
categories.target_behavior: Respect downside risk and current liquidity rather than optimistic continuation assumptions.
trap_behaviors: Overbid with thin cash.
Build into a dangerous board segment.
Assume rent income will arrive before debt pressure.
preferred_behaviors: Delay risk when board exposure is dangerous.
categories.scoring_notes: Cash-buffer and bid-cap rubrics act as overconfidence checks.
source_claims: Overconfidence can cause excessive risk-taking under uncertainty.

categories.title: Myopic Cash Preference
categories.description: Tests whether models hoard cash when an investment has strong strategic value.
categories.target_behavior: Spend cash when the Monopoly position justifies it and downside risk is manageable.
trap_behaviors: Decline cheap tempo acquisitions.
Avoid high-value building because it reduces cash today.
preferred_behaviors: Buy/build when the return justifies the liquidity reduction.
Balance cash buffer against monopoly conversion.
categories.scoring_notes: Rubrics reward high-tempo buys/builds when cash remains adequate.
source_claims: Myopic loss/cash preference can overweight immediate liquidity relative to long-term value.

categories.title: Recency And Availability Bias
categories.description: Tests whether recent rent danger or visible opponent threat causes excessive defensive play.
categories.target_behavior: Use current board probabilities and portfolio value rather than salient recent shocks.
trap_behaviors: Overreact to a recent rent hit.
Avoid all investment after one visible threat.
preferred_behaviors: Preserve cash only when the actual current risk justifies it.
Continue strategic investment when risk is manageable.
categories.scoring_notes: First-pass proxy category; more controlled paired fixtures are still needed.
source_claims: Availability bias can overweight recent or salient events.

categories.title: Fairness Bias
categories.description: Tests whether models overvalue equal-looking or polite trades at the expense of strategic edge.
categories.target_behavior: Reject fair-looking trades that are strategically bad and accept asymmetric trades that improve win odds.
trap_behaviors: Accept face-value fairness when it empowers a leader.
Reject advantageous asymmetry because it appears unfair.
preferred_behaviors: Evaluate trade consequences by monopoly creation, cash, and opponent strength.
categories.scoring_notes: Deterministic trade score is available, but fairness framing labels require human review.
source_claims: Fairness preferences can affect bargaining decisions even when payoff-maximizing choices differ.

categories.title: Coalition Or Anti-Leader Bias
categories.description: Tests whether anti-leader pressure causes strategically useful or excessive blocking behavior.
categories.target_behavior: Block leaders when it improves focal win odds without sacrificing too much value.
trap_behaviors: Overpay just to hurt the leader.
Reject profitable actions because they also help a leader.
preferred_behaviors: Compare anti-leader value against focal net-worth and survival impact.
categories.scoring_notes: Model intent and coalition framing require human review; deterministic score captures only action quality.
source_claims: Coalition and leader-blocking dynamics are common in multi-agent games and bargaining settings.

prompt_pipeline.note: Bias-v1 is a research-only overlay and is never injected into model-facing prompts.
